headline: An Iran-linked cyberattack knocked a British power plant offline for four days, the day's sharpest sign that state hackers now reach past data theft into physical infrastructure.

emerging_trends.text: State-linked hackers are crossing from data theft into physical sabotage, as an Iran-linked group knocked a British power plant offline for four days.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Iran-Linked Cyberattack Shuts UK Power Plant

emerging_trends.text: Attackers are wielding AI to compress the window from disclosure to exploitation, and the Chinese-speaking crew UAT-10147 now leans on it to scale intrusions against web servers worldwide.
emerging_trends.topic_title: UAT-10147 Scales Server Attacks With AI

emerging_trends.text: Criminals and breach actors converged on the financial sector, exposing private-equity giant Apollo Global's data and standing up cloaked fake bank sites to harvest credentials.

topics.title: Iran-Linked Cyberattack Shuts UK Power Plant
topics.latest_developments: Iran-linked hackers knocked a United Kingdom power plant offline for four days, inflicting real-world operational disruption on Britain's distributed energy grid.
topics.summary: SecurityWeek reports that attackers tied to Iran shut down a British power plant for four days, raising alarm over the resilience of distributed energy infrastructure and the prospect of repeatable strikes. Operators of distributed energy assets should harden operational-technology networks and segment control systems.

sources.title: Iran-Linked Hackers Shut Down UK Power Plant for Four Days

topics.title: CISA Orders Emergency Zimbra Patching
topics.latest_developments: CISA ordered U.S. government agencies to patch the actively exploited Zimbra Collaboration Suite flaw CVE-2026-73570 within three days, escalating from last week's addition of the bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
topics.summary: The OS command-injection bug CVE-2026-73570 lets attackers run commands on Zimbra Collaboration Suite mail servers, and CISA's directive gives federal agencies three days to apply the fix. Administrators running Zimbra should patch immediately.

sources.title: CISA orders urgent patching of actively exploited Zimbra flaw

topics.title: UAT-10147 Scales Server Attacks With AI
topics.latest_developments: Researchers exposed UAT-10147, a Chinese-speaking cybercrime group that uses AI to scale attacks on Windows and Linux web servers worldwide, deploying the SPECTRE implant with an EDR bypass and a Linux rootkit.
topics.summary: UAT-10147 hits education, media, technology, and gaming organizations concentrated in Brazil, Bolivia, China, Canada, and Vietnam, uncovered after investigators found an exposed attacker directory. Web-server operators should hunt for SPECTRE, EDR tampering, and rootkit activity.

sources.title: UAT-10147 Uses AI to Scale Server Attacks, Deploys SPECTRE With EDR Bypass and Linux Rootkit

topics.title: Chameleon SEO Poisoning Fakes Bank Sites
topics.latest_developments: Fortra's threat-intelligence unit FIRE named Chameleon SEO Poisoning, a technique that ranks cloaked fake banking websites for high-intent search terms and makes them play dead to slip past scanners, and logged a 40% jump in cases during the second quarter of 2026.
topics.summary: Chameleon SEO Poisoning manipulates search results to steer victims to counterfeit bank login pages that harvest credentials while dodging automated crawlers. Banks and their customers should verify URLs and distrust search-ranked login links.

sources.title: Fake bank websites play dead to evade security scanners

topics.title: Record ATM Jackpotting Sentence
topics.latest_developments: A federal court sentenced Venezuelan national Juan Manuel Gouveia-Aguilera to eight years in prison, a record term, for an ATM jackpotting scheme that caused millions of dollars in losses.
topics.summary: Gouveia-Aguilera helped run jackpotting attacks that force ATMs to spit out cash on command, draining machines of millions. The sentence marks the longest U.S. federal prison term for the crime.

sources.title: Venezuelan Gets Record Federal Prison Term for ATM Jackpotting

topics.title: Apollo Global Data Breach
topics.latest_developments: Private equity firm Apollo Global Management disclosed a breach that exposed personal information, part of a campaign that targets major financial companies.
topics.summary: SecurityWeek reports intruders lifted personal data from Apollo Global Management in what appears to be a broader push against large financial firms. Affected individuals should watch for fraud and phishing tied to the exposure.

sources.title: Personal Information Exposed in Apollo Global Data Breach

business_politics.title: Treasury's 'Economic D-Day' on Iran
business_politics.latest_developments: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will unveil new sanctions on Iran on August 24, and Tehran threatened to fine or confiscate 46 ships it says violated Strait of Hormuz transit rules.
business_politics.summary: The Trump administration is moving to intensify financial pressure on Iran to force concessions as talks stall, a step markets are calling an economic D-Day; oil fell more than 1.5% ahead of the announcement while gold climbed above $4,700 an ounce.

sources.title: FirstFT: An economic D-Day is coming for Iran
Iran threatens 46 ships in Strait of Hormuz transit crackdown
Oil Falls Ahead of Bessent’s Press Conference

business_politics.title: U.S.-Canada Trade Talks Collapse
business_politics.latest_developments: The Wall Street Journal reported August 24 that U.S.-Canada trade talks have formally failed, hardening the tariff standoff a day after Ottawa set fresh retaliatory levies.
business_politics.summary: The United States and Canada, each other's largest trading partners, are spiraling toward a full trade war after 50% U.S. tariffs took effect and Prime Minister Mark Carney held to his 'no deal is better than a bad deal' doctrine, which draws broad support across Canada's political spectrum.

sources.title: Canada’s Carney Puts His ‘No Deal Is Better Than a Bad Deal’ Doctrine to the Test

business.title: Homer City Boom May Fund Indiana County Broadband
business.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette report August 24 finds the economic boom around the former Homer City coal plant could finally extend affordable high-speed internet across Indiana County.
business.summary: Redevelopment at the shuttered Homer City Generating Station in Indiana County is building momentum that officials hope will pull long-underserved rural areas into modern broadband access and affordability.

sources.title: An economic boom may pull Indiana County internet access into the future

business.title: Cost of Living Comfortably in Pittsburgh Climbs
business.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette analysis August 24 reports the income needed to live comfortably in Pittsburgh has risen steeply.
business.summary: The Post-Gazette found the price of living comfortably in Pittsburgh is climbing, squeezing household budgets across the region even as the city keeps its reputation for affordability.

sources.title: The price of living comfortably in Pittsburgh is getting steep

around_town.title: PRT Ridership Rises 5%
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh Regional Transit reported ridership climbed 5%, the Post-Gazette said August 24.
around_town.summary: Pittsburgh Regional Transit's ridership rose 5% as riders return to buses and light rail across Allegheny County, a gain the agency touts amid its broader Bus Line Refresh planning.

sources.title: Numbers boost: Pittsburgh Regional Transit ridership up 5%

around_town.title: Pittsburgh's Teen-Access Limits Draw Scrutiny
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource reported August 24 that Pittsburgh officials will not explain how they decided to restrict teens' access to some public spaces this summer.
around_town.summary: Fears of 'teen takeovers' led Pittsburgh to limit youth access to certain public spaces over the summer, and PublicSource found city officials tight-lipped about who made those calls and how, raising transparency questions.

sources.title: Pittsburgh’s summer of teen restrictions raises transparency questions

around_town.title: Pennsylvania Schools Brace for Measles
around_town.latest_developments: A Post-Gazette report August 24 details how area schools are preparing as measles spreads across Pennsylvania and classes resume.
around_town.summary: With measles cases climbing statewide and the first Allegheny County case since 2019 confirmed at UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania schools are checking vaccination records and readiness for the new year.

sources.title: Measles is overtaking Pennsylvania. How are schools preparing?

events.title: Sweetwater Arts Center Open House
events.latest_developments: TribLive reported August 24 that Sweetwater Center for the Arts in Sewickley will hold a public open house August 29.
events.summary: Sweetwater Center for the Arts hosts an open house Saturday, August 29, 2026, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. at its Sewickley campus, inviting the public to tour its classes and studios.

sources.title: Sweetwater Center for the Arts to host an open house Aug. 29

team_usa.title: Rose Lavelle Leaves With Head Injury
team_usa.latest_developments: U.S. international Rose Lavelle left Gotham FC's scoreless draw with Angel City FC in the first half August 23 with a head injury, ESPN reported.
team_usa.summary: Gotham FC midfielder Rose Lavelle, a mainstay of the U.S. women's national team, came off in the first half of a scoreless NWSL draw against Angel City FC because of a head injury, an added worry for the USWNT.

sources.title: U.S. international Lavelle suffers head injury
